Aurva
(‘born from the thigh’)
------------------------------------------
Son of the sage च्यवन (a descendant of भृगु) and Āruṣi (daughter of मनु), और्व got this name since he was born from the ūru or the thigh of his मोथेर्. Once, the kṣattriyas belonging to the race of कार्तवीर्यार्जुन were harassing the ṛṣis who were descendants of भृगु, including the womenfolk. As a result of the tension and fear, the foetus in the womb of Āruṣi slipped into her thigh and was born out of it. The child—ṛṣi Aurva—stared at the marauders making them blind. They regained their sight by praying to the child-sage.
Later on, the sage और्व engaged himself in a sacrifice aimed at destroying the followers of कार्तवीर्यार्जुन. He was however dissuaded from doing so. In the process और्व discharged his anger into the sea, in the form of a horse. This submarine fire came to be known as ‘Vaḍavāgni.’
Aurva had two children: ऋचीक (son) and Kandalī (daughter).
See also CYAVANA.
